cases.proves_bugs: BUG-784 (window half: the FROM column of the Pit Schedule window keeps "C5" and "C6", and two such inlets at the same level stay two rows; the after-command refresh of a drawn table, ScheduleLinkService.cs 2677 and 2701, is NOT driven)
cases.title: Two pipes into P11 from pits named C5 and C6, both arriving at the same level: the Pit Schedule FROM column reads C5 and C6 on two rows, never "C" or "Cs"
cases.plan_item: BUG-784 proof (wave 1, group S, job S3): Pit Schedule FROM column keeps the number of a pit not named P + digits
cases.expected: PIT three times with the number typed in New Pit (C5 at 150000,-80000, C6 at 170000,-60000, P11 at 170000,-80000; cover 19.000; three Esc each) puts 'Pit placed successfully.' on the command line three times. CD C5 to P11 and CD C6 to P11, each 18.000 / 17.800, open no Grade mismatch window and each put a 'was 225 mm inside the pit' line on the command line. The Pit Schedule then shows P11's group with one row FROM C5 and one row FROM C6; no row of P11's group reads FROM C or Cs.
cases.why_not_unit: The FROM text comes from the live window reading the real pits and pipes CE recorded in the drawing, with the real Settings switch; a unit test already covers BuildInletFromDisplay, but not that the window uses it on a drawing.
not_automated: The drawn Pit Schedule table (the after-command refresh of a FROM cell) is not driven: placing these rows in the drawn table needs 'Place schedule' or a proven 'Update existing schedule' route, and reading drawn cells is unproven on DRV1_B1. A Codex look covers it (report section 1).
Names CP3, SPS1 and an X-Civil GP4 are not typed; the rule is the same for any letters that are not a source tag. That a downpipe (DP1) still reads "DP" is not driven here.
The inlet levels in P11's rows are recorded, not asserted (the cell format of a new pipe's level is not yet seen on a run).
